claims.text: Adaptive enhanced sampling using replica exchange or metadynamics-guided intermediate-state selection will significantly improve reference–target phase-space overlap for ab initio liquids in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Equimolar multicomponent high-entropy alloys can occur as solid and liquid states near their high melting temperatures.
The liquid phase of a multicomponent high-entropy alloy has a vast array of atomic configurations.
Replica exchange or metadynamics can be used to dynamically select and adjust intermediate states during thermodynamic integration.
Thermodynamic integration can be used to obtain configurational free energies for multicomponent alloys.
The intervention applies to high-entropy alloys containing five or more metallic elements.
The applicable temperature range is approximately 2000 K to 3600 K.
Dynamically generated intermediate configurations will bridge the configurational gap between a simplified EAM reference ensemble and the ab initio liquid.
Continuous adaptation of intermediate-state sampling will represent the full ensemble of liquid atomic configurations more accurately.
More accurate sampling of intermediate states will make the reference system better mirror the fluctuations and configurational diversity of the target liquid.
The adaptive method will improve phase-space-overlap efficacy by approximately tens of percent.
The adaptive method will yield free-energy convergence closer to true ab initio values than conventional TOR-TILD EAM references.
Conventional TOR-TILD EAM references inadequately capture the variety of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid.
The intervention will be most effective for equimolar multicomponent systems near their melting points.
The benefits of adaptive sampling will diminish for binary systems or at substantially lower temperatures because their configurational landscapes are less complex.
A controlled comparison of conventional TOR-TILD EAM references with adaptive enhanced sampling can test the proposed improvement.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in free-energy integration mismatch and improved benchmark agreement would falsify the hypothesis.
